correctness.rationale: Weyl operators orthogonally diagonalize the analysis Gram matrix, so rank equals the number of nonzero ambiguity coefficients, with singular values squared p|A_g|². Cyclotomic irreducibility of 1+X+...+X^{p-1} makes a p-term phase sum zero exactly for a permutation of the prime field. Centering a nonzero translation of cx^5+dx^3+ex yields Ay^4+By²+Dy with A=5ca, B=(5/2)ca³+3da, D=-b. For p≡1 mod4, the m=(p-1)/4 power sum forces A=0; p≡3 mod4≥11, m=(p+1)/4 forces B=0 and t=(p+5)/4 forces D=0, leaving a noninjective even quartic. At p=7, power sums force B=0 and (D/A)^2=2, and explicit value lists show both possibilities sufficient: d=5ca² and b=±ca give exactly four additional zero Weyl indices when d/c∈{3,5,6}. p≤5 is checked with x^p=x and nonpermuting quadratics. Independent exact finite-field enumeration over every (c,d,a,b) for primes 2,3,5,7,11,13 passed, including precisely 18 exceptional pairs at p=7. The all-prime claim depends on these power-sum proofs, not enumeration.
